questions.question: From the alternatives given below, choose the correct meaning of the idiom 'think the world of someone'.

options.text: To like and admire them very much, or to have a very high opinion of them
To hate and reject someone and refuse to talk to them
Interfere in the life of someone and try to trouble him
Think of destroying the world of someone

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **To like and admire them very much, or to have a very high opinion of them**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **'think the world of someone'** means to have a very high opinion of someone or to love and admire them deeply. (किसी को बहुत अधिक पसंद करना या उसका बहुत सम्मान करना)
 
 
• **Example: **Ever since he helped the community during the crisis, the residents **think the world of him**.
 
 
 
• **'To like and admire them very much, or to have a very high opinion of them'** refers to the act of holding someone in extremely high regard or having deep affection for them. (किसी को बहुत पसंद करना और उसका बहुत सम्मान करना)
 
 
• **Example: **She **thinks the world of her elder brother** because he has always supported her dreams.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can conclude that the idiom is used to express **great admiration** or **love**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **To like and admire them very much, or to have a very high opinion of them**.

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To hate and reject someone** (किसी से नफरत करना और उसे त्याग देना): To feel intense dislike for a person and refuse to accept or speak to them.
 
 
• **Example: **After the betrayal, he decided to **hate and reject** his former business partner.
 
 
 
• **Interfere in the life of someone** (किसी के जीवन में हस्तक्षेप करना): To get involved in someone else's private matters without being asked, often causing trouble.
 
 
• **Example: **It is better to focus on your own goals rather than **interfere in the life of someone** else.
 
 
 
• **Think of destroying the world of someone** (किसी की दुनिया तबाह करने की सोचना): To have malicious intentions to ruin someone's happiness, career, or personal life.
 
 
• **Example: **In the story, the jealous rival would constantly **think of destroying the world** of the successful protagonist.

questions.question: From the alternatives given below, choose the correct meaning of the idiom 'a dime a dozen'.

options.text: So scarce as to hold high value
So abundant or common as to hold little or no value
Sold only in exchange of a dime

questions.solution: Question 1 The correct answer is: **So abundant or common as to hold little or no value**. **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **'a dime a dozen'** refers to something that is very **common**, **easy to find**, and therefore **not very valuable** or special. (**बहुत ही साधारण या कौड़ी के भाव मिलने वाला**) • **Example: **In that city, people with basic computer skills are **a dime a dozen**. • **'So abundant or common as to hold little or no value'** accurately describes the essence of this idiom, highlighting that **excessive availability** leads to a **decrease in worth**. (**बहुत प्रचुर या आम होने के कारण बहुत कम या कोई मूल्य न होना**) • **Example: **Cheap plastic phone cases are **so abundant or common as to hold little or no value** in the resale market. • Hence, we can infer that the correct meaning of the idiom **'a dime a dozen'** is **'so abundant or common as to hold little or no value'**. Therefore, the correct answer is: **So abundant or common as to hold little or no value**. **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **So scarce as to hold high value** (**दुर्लभ और बहुत कीमती**): Refers to things that are **rare** and thus very **expensive**, which is the opposite of the given idiom. • **Example: **Flawless blue diamonds are **so scarce as to hold high value** across the globe. • **Produced in large quantity** (**बड़ी मात्रा में उत्पादित**): Refers to **mass production**, which may lead to being common, but it doesn't necessarily define the idiom's focus on **low value**. • **Example: **Generic medicines are **produced in large quantity** to ensure they reach everyone. • **Sold only in exchange of a dime** (**केवल एक डाइम के बदले में बेची गई**): This is a **literal interpretation** of the words in the idiom, which is incorrect as idioms have **figurative meanings**. • **Example: **Decades ago, small candies were often **sold only in exchange of a dime**. 35:Td1a, The correct answer is: **To like and admire them very much, or to have a very high opinion of them**.

questions.question: Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following. An extreme fear of dirt and germs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mysophobia**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Mysophobia** is defined as an intense, pathological, and irrational **fear of dirt**, **germs**, and **contamination**.

• The term was first introduced to medical literature by **William Alexander Hammond** in **1879** when he was describing a specific manifestation of **Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD)** characterized by a patient's need for constant handwashing.

• Etymologically, the word is derived from the Greek words **mysos**, meaning **uncleanness** or **impurity**, and **phobos**, meaning **fear**.

• Individuals with **Mysophobia**, often called **germaphobes**, frequently engage in ritualistic behaviors such as **excessive cleaning**, wearing **gloves** or masks in public, and the compulsive use of **sanitizers** to avoid **bacteria** and **viruses**.

• Severe cases can lead to significant social isolation, as the individual may avoid public transport, restaurants, or physical contact (like **handshakes**) to mitigate the perceived risk of **infection**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Trypanophobia**:

• It is the extreme and irrational **fear of needles** or **medical injections**.

• It is recognized as a specific phobia in the **DSM-5** and often results in a **vasovagal response**, which may cause the patient to faint or experience a sharp drop in blood pressure.

• **Hemophobia**:

• This refers to the intense **fear of blood**, whether it is seeing their own blood, the blood of others, or even images of blood.

• Similar to **Trypanophobia**, it is distinct from other phobias because it often triggers a **vasovagal syncope** rather than a typical fight-or-flight anxiety response.

• **Dentophobia**:

• It is the overwhelming **fear of dentists** or **dental treatments**.

• This condition often leads to the complete avoidance of **oral healthcare**, which can result in severe **dental decay** and gum disease due to the anxiety surrounding **dental drills** and **local anesthesia**.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
Several cultural exchange programmes are organised by the council every summer to promote international understanding.

options.text: The council organises several cultural exchange programmes every summer to promote international understanding.
The council organised several cultural exchange programmes every summer to promote international understanding.
The council is organising several cultural exchange programmes every summer to promote international understanding.
The council will organise several cultural exchange programmes every summer to promote international understanding.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The council organises several cultural exchange programmes every summer to promote international understanding**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is in the **Passive Voice** because the recipient of the action (Several cultural exchange programmes) is placed in the subject position, and the agent (the council) follows the preposition **by**.

• To convert a sentence from **Passive Voice** to **Active Voice**, the **Object** of the passive sentence ('the council') must become the **Subject** of the active sentence.

• The original sentence is in the **Simple Present Tense**, as indicated by the auxiliary verb **are** followed by the past participle **organised**, and the adverbial phrase **every summer** which signifies a habitual action.

• In the **Active Voice** structure for the **Simple Present Tense**, the verb follows the formula: **Subject + V1 (s/es) + Object**.

• Since the new subject **the council** is a **singular collective noun**, the verb must take the **-s** suffix, changing **organised** back to its base form **organises**.

• The phrase **every summer to promote international understanding** remains as a modifier to provide context regarding frequency and purpose.

 **Additional Information__**

• Comparison with other options:

• **Simple Past Tense**: Option 2 uses **organised**, which would be the active form of **were organised**. It indicates a completed action in the past rather than a recurring habit.

• **Present Continuous Tense**: Option 3 uses **is organising**, which represents an action currently in progress. The passive equivalent would be **are being organised**.

• **Simple Future Tense**: Option 4 uses **will organise**, which refers to an action that will happen later. The passive equivalent would be **will be organised**.

• **Habitual Aspect**: Phrases like **every summer**, **usually**, or **always** typically require the **Simple Present Tense** to denote regularity or universal truths.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
Let the work not be delayed any further.

options.text: Don't delay the work any further.
The work not be delay any further.
You cannot delay the work any further.
The work shouldn't be delayed any further.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Don't delay the work any further.**__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The provided sentence 'Let the work not be delayed any further' is in the **Passive Voice** and is categorized as an **Imperative Sentence** expressing a command or instruction.
 
• In **Imperative Sentences**, the passive structure 'Let + object + not + be + Past Participle (V3)' is converted into the active structure 'Do not (Don't) + Base Verb (V1) + object'.
 
• In this specific case, **'the work'** acts as the object, and **'delayed'** is the past participle form of the verb **'delay'**.
 
• When shifting to the **Active Voice**, the hidden subject **'You'** is understood but typically omitted in imperative commands. The sentence starts with the **negative auxiliary** 'Don't' followed by the **base form** of the verb 'delay'.
 
• The phrase 'any further' remains an **adverbial adjunct** at the end of the sentence to maintain the original meaning and intensity of the instruction.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Voice Transformation Rules:**
 
 
• **Positive Imperative:** Active (V1 + Object) becomes Passive (Let + Object + be + V3). For example, 'Finish the task' becomes 'Let the task be finished'.
 
• **Negative Imperative:** Active (Don't + V1 + Object) becomes Passive (Let + Object + not + be + V3). This matches the structure of the given question.
 
 
 
• **Evaluation of Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **The work not be delay any further:** This is grammatically incorrect as it lacks a proper **finite verb** or auxiliary structure.
 
• **You cannot delay the work any further:** This changes the **mood** of the sentence from a command (imperative) to a statement regarding **ability** or **permission** (modal).
 
• **The work shouldn't be delayed any further:** This sentence is still in the **Passive Voice**, indicated by the 'be + delayed' construction, and uses the **modal verb** 'should' to give advice rather than a direct command.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

Sir Charles Wilkins translated the Bhagavad Geeta from Sanskrit ___ English.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**into**'. **__Key Points__** __ 
• The preposition **into** is used to indicate a **change of state**, **form**, or **medium**. 
• In the context of languages, the verb **translate** is typically followed by the preposition **from** (for the source language) and **into** (for the target language). 
• The sentence specifies that the text was moved from one medium (**Sanskrit**) to another (**English**), making **into** the grammatically correct choice. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**. **Complete Sentence:** *'Sir Charles Wilkins translated the Bhagavad Geeta from Sanskrit **into**__ English.'* **__Additional Information__** 
• **Option 1: through** is used to indicate movement from one side to another or a means of doing something, but it is not used for language translation. 
• **Option 2: to** is sometimes used in informal speech, but **into** is the standard preposition for indicating a transformation or translation of content. 
• **Option 3: in** refers to a static state (e.g., 'The book is written in English') rather than the process of changing from one language to another. 
• **Sir Charles Wilkins** (1749−1836) was an English typographer and Orientalist who famously produced the first direct English translation of the **Bhagavad Gita** in **1785**. </ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."
The new policy was believing to have reduced corruption in the department.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**was believed to have reduced**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The subject of the sentence is **The new policy**, which is an inanimate object. An inanimate object cannot perform the cognitive action of **believing**. Therefore, the **active voice** (was believing) is logically incorrect, and the sentence requires a **passive voice** construction (was believed).

• The phrase **to have reduced** is a **perfect infinitive**. This grammatical structure is used to indicate an action that occurred prior to the time of the main verb. In this sentence, it signifies that the **reduction of corruption** is a completed action relative to the time people held the belief.

• The **past passive** form **was believed** correctly establishes the timeframe of the public or departmental opinion, while the **perfect infinitive** properly links it to the preceding outcome of the policy.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Passive Voice Mechanics**:

• In English grammar, the **passive voice** is formed using the auxiliary verb **to be** followed by the **past participle** (V3) of the main verb. Here, **was** (be-verb) + **believed** (V3) correctly shifts the focus to the policy as the object of belief.

• **Stative Verbs and Continuous Tense**:

• The verb **believe** is a **stative verb** (expressing a state of mind). Stative verbs are generally not used in **continuous tenses** (e.g., was believing, is being believed) in formal standard English, making such options grammatically weak.

• **Simple vs. Perfect Infinitive**:

• A **simple infinitive** (to reduce) usually refers to the same time as the main verb or a future time. A **perfect infinitive** (to have reduced) refers to a time earlier than the main verb. Given the context of a policy already showing results, the **perfect infinitive** is the most precise choice.

</ul

A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."
An amicable reconciliation could not be achieved during the mediation process as the parties did nothing but accused each other.

options.text: did anything but accuse each other
did nothing but accuse each other

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence contains a grammatical error in the use of the **past tense** ('accused') after the phrase '**did nothing but**'.
 
• When the word '**but**' is used as a preposition meaning '**except**' following any form of the auxiliary verb '**do**' (do, does, did), it must be followed by a **bare infinitive** (the base form of the verb without 'to').
 
• Therefore, the verb '**accused**' should be replaced with its base form, '**accuse**'.
 
• The correct idiomatic expression is '**did nothing but accuse**', which emphasizes that the only action the parties took was accusing one another.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'An amicable reconciliation could not be achieved during the mediation process as the parties **did nothing but accuse each other**.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: 'did anything but accuse'** – The phrase 'anything but' means 'not at all' or 'by no means'. This would imply the parties did **not** accuse each other, which contradicts the context that reconciliation failed.
 
• **Option 2: 'did not accuse each other'** – This changes the intended meaning of the sentence. If they did not accuse each other, it does not explain why an amicable reconciliation could **not** be achieved.
 
• **Option 4: 'No improvement required'** – This is incorrect because 'accused' is grammatically incompatible with the 'did nothing but' construction.
</ul

questions.question: Choose the correct form of verb to fill in blank (A).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**introduces**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• The sentence describes a regular or repeated action indicated by the phrase '**year after year**'. 
• For habitual actions or general truths, we use the **Simple Present Tense**. 
• The subject '**The company**' is a **singular** third-person noun. 
• According to the rules of **subject-verb agreement**, a singular subject in the simple present tense takes a verb ending in '**s**' or '**es**'. 
• '**Introduces**' is the only option that correctly follows this grammatical rule. Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'. Complete Passage: *In today's world, brands are more than just names; they represent trust, quality, and identity. For example, when people hear the name Apple, they immediately think of sleek design and innovation. The company 1. introduces__ new technology year after year, setting global trends in smartphones, laptops, and wearables. Similarly, Nike is not only about shoes but also about motivation. Its slogan 'Just Do It' 2. __inspires__ millions of athletes to push their limits. The brand has become a symbol of determination and energy. On the other hand, Coca-Cola has maintained its popularity for decades. Advertisements of the brand 3. __are associated with__ happiness, friendship, and celebration. People often associate drinking Coke with moments of joy. However, brands also face criticism. Fast fashion brands, for instance, are accused of producing cheap clothes that harm the environment. If companies continue like this, they 4. __Wil__ lose customer trust in the future. It is important to remember that a brand is 5. __not built overnight__. It is built through years of consistency, customer care, and innovation. Truly famous brands survive not only because of advertising but because they deliver value again and again.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• '**Introduce**' is the plural form of the verb and does not match the singular subject 'The company'. 
• '**Introduced**' is the past tense, which does not fit the context of a recurring present action. 
• '**Will introducing**' is grammatically incorrect as the modal verb 'will' must be followed by the base form of the verb (will introduce) or 'be' + '-ing' (will be introducing). </ul

questions.question: Choose the correct verb form to fill in blank (B).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**inspires**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• The sentence requires a **transitive verb** to connect the subject (the slogan) with the object (millions of athletes). 
• The subject '**Its slogan "Just Do It"**' is **singular**, so the verb must also be in the singular form, which is '**inspires**'. 
• In the construction '**inspires someone to do something**', the verb is followed directly by the object (millions of athletes) without any intervening preposition. 
• Therefore, '**inspires**' is the grammatically correct choice to show the direct impact of the slogan on the athletes. Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'. Complete Passage: *In today's world, brands are more than just names; they represent trust, quality, and identity. For example, when people hear the name Apple, they immediately think of sleek design and innovation. The company 1. **introduces**__ new technology year after year, setting global trends in smartphones, laptops, and wearables. Similarly, **Nike** is not only about shoes but also about motivation. Its slogan 'Just Do It' 2. __**inspires**__ millions of athletes to push their limits. The brand has become a symbol of determination and energy. On the other hand, **Coca-Cola** has maintained its popularity for decades. Advertisements of the brand 3. __**are associated with**__ happiness, friendship, and celebration. People often associate drinking Coke with moments of joy. However, brands also face criticism. Fast fashion brands, for instance, are accused of producing cheap clothes that harm the environment. If companies continue like this, they 4. __**Wil**__ lose customer trust in the future. It is important to remember that a brand is 5. __**not built overnight**__. It is built through years of consistency, customer care, and innovation. Truly famous brands survive not only because of advertising but because they deliver value again and again.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• **inspires to**: This is incorrect because the preposition 'to' should come after the object (e.g., inspires athletes **to** push), not immediately after the verb. 
• **inspires at / inspires over**: These prepositions do not logically or grammatically fit the relationship between a slogan and the people it motivates. </ul

questions.question: Choose the correct modal verb to fill in blank (D).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Wil**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• The sentence in blank (D) follows the structure of the **First Conditional**. 
• The **First Conditional** is used to talk about possibilities in the present or in the future that are likely to happen. 
• The structure is: **If + Simple Present, Will + Base Verb**. 
• In the given passage, the 'if-clause' is 'If companies **continue** like this' (Simple Present). 
• Therefore, the main clause requires a future modal like '**will**' to express the certain consequence in the future. 
• Despite the typographical variation, '**Wil**' serves as the intended modal verb to complete the future prediction. Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'. Complete Passage: *In today's world, brands are more than just names; they represent trust, quality, and identity. For example, when people hear the name Apple, they immediately think of sleek design and innovation. The company 1. **introduces**__ new technology year after year, setting global trends in smartphones, laptops, and wearables. Similarly, Nike is not only about shoes but also about motivation. Its slogan 'Just Do It' 2. __**inspires**__ millions of athletes to push their limits. The brand has become a symbol of determination and energy. On the other hand, Coca-Cola has maintained its popularity for decades. Advertisements of the brand 3. __**are associated with**__ happiness, friendship, and celebration. People often associate drinking Coke with moments of joy. However, brands also face criticism. Fast fashion brands, for instance, are accused of producing cheap clothes that harm the environment. If companies continue like this, they 4. __**Wil**__ lose customer trust in the future. It is important to remember that a brand is 5. __**not built overnight**__. It is built through years of consistency, customer care, and innovation. Truly famous brands survive not only because of advertising but because they deliver value again and again.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• **Should**: Generally used to give **advice** or express an **obligation**. It does not fit the cause-and-effect prediction of the first conditional here. 
• **Would**: Used in the **Second Conditional** (If + Simple Past, Would + Base Verb) to talk about hypothetical or unlikely situations. Since the condition is in the present (continue), 'would' is grammatically incorrect. 
• **Shal**: A misspelling of 'shall'. **Shall** is typically used with first-person subjects (I/We) in formal contexts and is less common for future predictions with 'they'. </ul

questions.question: What does the idiom in (E): (not built overnight) mean?

options.text: Something that is completed very quickly
Something that takes time and effort to develop

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Something that takes time and effort to develop**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ 
• The idiom '**not built overnight**' is a variation of the common phrase '**Rome wasn't built in a day**'. 
• It is used to emphasize that important achievements, reputations, or large-scale projects require a significant amount of **time**, **patience**, and **persistent effort** to reach completion or success. 
• In the context of the passage, the author explains that a **brand** is the result of **years of consistency**, **customer care**, and **innovation**, which directly supports the idea that it cannot be created quickly. 
• Therefore, '**Something that takes time and effort to develop**' is the most accurate definition. Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'. Complete Passage: *In today’s world, brands are more than just names; they represent trust, quality, and identity. For example, when people hear the name **Apple**, they immediately think of sleek design and innovation. The company 1. **introduces**__ new technology year after year, setting global trends in smartphones, laptops, and wearables. Similarly, **Nike** is not only about shoes but also about motivation. Its slogan **“Just Do It”** 2. __**inspires**__ millions of athletes to push their limits. The brand has become a symbol of determination and energy. On the other hand, **Coca-Cola** has maintained its popularity for decades. Advertisements of the brand 3. __**are associated with**__ happiness, friendship, and celebration. People often associate drinking Coke with moments of joy. However, brands also face criticism. **Fast fashion** brands, for instance, are accused of producing cheap clothes that harm the environment. If companies continue like this, they 4. __**will**__ lose customer trust in the future. It is important to remember that a brand is 5. __**not built overnight**__. It is built through years of consistency, customer care, and innovation. Truly famous brands survive not only because of advertising but because they deliver value again and again.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
• **Something that is completed very quickly:** This is the opposite of what the idiom implies. Success usually requires a long-term commitment. 
• **Something that appears by chance:** This refers to luck or accidents, whereas building a brand requires **deliberate planning** and **hard work**. 
• **Something that is destroyed suddenly:** This refers to a quick downfall or failure, which does not relate to the **constructive process** mentioned in the text.
